objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to identify and write complete sentences and apply six capitalization rules in their academic writing.
materials: - Coursebook: First Steps in Academic Writing, pp 10-18

stages.stage_aim: To activate learners' awareness of their own writing errors and establish why accurate sentences and capitalization matter for exam success
stages.procedure:
- Ask Ss: "What's your biggest problem with grammar when you write in English?" Pairs discuss. 2 min. Elicit ideas — guide toward punctuation, grammar, capital letters.
- Teacher explains: "I've analyzed your recent writing. Two patterns keep appearing — sentences that aren't complete, and missing capital letters. These are the errors costing you marks."
- Display the PET Writing assessment scale on screen. Use auto-animate to zoom in on the Organization and Language bands. Explain: "If your sentences aren't complete and capitals are missing, you can't score above Band 2 in Organization or Language. Getting this right is the fastest way to raise your writing score."

stages.stage_aim: To gauge how accurately learners can distinguish complete sentences from fragments before any teaching input
stages.procedure:
- Display 8 word groups on screen: a mix of complete sentences, fragments, and command sentences. Ss work individually: mark each ✓ (sentence) or ✗ (not a sentence). 3 min.
- Pair check — but do NOT give answers yet. 2 min.
- Teacher surveys results (mini whiteboards or hands up) to identify which items caused most confusion. This determines what the Teach phase focuses on.

stages.stage_aim: To assess which capitalization rules learners already apply correctly and which need explicit instruction
stages.procedure:
- Display a short paragraph with 12 capitalization errors on screen. Ss underline letters that should be capitals. 3 min.
- Pair check — do NOT reveal answers yet. 2 min.
- Teacher notes which rules students missed most (the pronoun I? nationalities? place names?). This shapes the Teach phase.

stages.stage_aim: To clarify the sentence definition and present the six capitalization rules, targeting only the areas the diagnostics exposed as weak
stages.procedure:
- Sentences (5 min): Display the definition — a sentence must have a subject, a verb, and express a complete thought. Use 2–3 examples from Test 1 to illustrate each criterion. Show why each fragment fails. Introduce command sentences as the exception (subject 'you' is understood). Quick check: Ss complete Practice 2A (Commands, p. 12) — identify the two command sentences and underline their verbs. Elicit further examples from Ss.
- Capitalization (5 min): Display the six rules on screen one at a time. For each rule, reference the correct answer from Test 2 as an example. Spend extra time on rules students missed most in the diagnostic. Quick oral check: "What do we capitalize? Give me an example."

stages.stage_aim: To give learners structured practice in applying the sentence definition and articulating the reason each fragment is incomplete
stages.procedure:
- Ss open books to Practice 2 — Recognizing Sentences, Part B (p. 12). Pairs work through all 13 items: mark each S or NS, and write the reason for each NS item. Demo item 1 together. 8 min.
- Whole-class feedback: for each NS item, nominate a different pair to explain why — no subject? no verb? incomplete thought?

stages.stage: Freer Practice — Practice 7: Editing for Capitalization
stages.stage_aim: To give learners extended practice applying all six capitalization rules to an authentic paragraph
stages.procedure:
- Ss turn to Practice 7 — Editing for Capitalization (p. 18). Working individually, read the Nelson Mandela paragraph and change small letters to capitals wherever necessary. Remind them to consider all six rules. 5 min.
- Pair check, then whole-class feedback — display the corrected paragraph on screen. Discuss any disagreements.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate the two core concepts and connect progress back to the PET writing criteria introduced at the start
stages.procedure:
- Quick-fire quiz: "What three things must a complete sentence have?" "Name four things that need a capital letter in English."
- Return to the PET Writing scale: "Now that you can write complete sentences and capitalize correctly, which Organization and Language bands are you reaching?"
- Preview Part 2: "Next lesson — what's inside a sentence? Subjects, verbs, and objects."
